primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ATP7B loss impairs biliary copper excretion and copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin, causing toxic copper accumulation in liver, brain, and cornea.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has tremor, personality change, elevated aminotransferases, and Kayser-Fleischer rings. Genetic testing identifies biallelic ATP7B variants.
lead: Which physiologic process is most directly impaired?
correct: Hepatic excretion of copper into bile
distractor_notes: Excess intestinal iron absorption characterizes hereditary hemochromatosis, not Wilson disease.
Cystine reabsorption defects cause cystinuria and recurrent stones.
Sphingomyelin degradation defects cause acid sphingomyelinase deficiency.
Hepatic LDL uptake is impaired in familial hypercholesterolemia and is unrelated to ATP7B.
key_expl: ATP7B is required for biliary copper excretion; loss causes copper retention and systemic toxicity.
objective: Explain Wilson disease through defective ATP7B-mediated biliary copper excretion.

sources.title: Wilson disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes Wilson disease as failure to eliminate excess copper, leading to accumulation in liver, brain, and other tissues.

sources.title: ATP7B gene
sources.support: ATP7B encodes a copper-transporting ATPase involved in copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin and excretion into bile.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: HFE-related dysregulation lowers hepcidin signaling and inappropriately increases intestinal iron absorption and iron release, causing progressive parenchymal iron overload.
vignette: A 52-year-old man has fatigue, diabetes mellitus, bronze skin pigmentation, hepatomegaly, high ferritin, and markedly elevated transferrin saturation. Genetic testing shows pathogenic HFE variants.
lead: Which physiologic abnormality most directly drives the progressive tissue injury?
correct: Excessive intestinal absorption of dietary iron
distractor_notes: Defective biliary copper excretion causes Wilson disease.
Transferrin deficiency would impair iron transport rather than produce classic HFE-associated systemic iron loading.
Excess urinary iron loss would deplete iron stores, not cause overload.
Heme oxygenase participates in heme catabolism and is not the primary abnormality in hereditary hemochromatosis.
key_expl: Hereditary hemochromatosis causes inappropriately high intestinal iron absorption and progressive iron deposition in organs.
objective: Connect HFE-related hemochromatosis with excessive intestinal iron absorption and systemic iron overload.
clues: high transferrin saturation with ferritin elevation
diabetes, skin pigmentation, and liver disease

sources.title: About Hereditary Hemochromatosis
sources.support: CDC describes hereditary hemochromatosis as excessive absorption and storage of iron that can damage liver, heart, pancreas, and other organs.

sources.title: HFE gene
sources.support: HFE participates in regulation of iron absorption; pathogenic variants are a major cause of hereditary hemochromatosis.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: An immune response to dietary gluten in genetically susceptible patients injures small-intestinal mucosa, causing villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and malabsorption.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has chronic diarrhea, abdominal bloating, weight loss, and iron deficiency anemia. Tissue transglutaminase IgA antibodies are strongly positive.
distractors: Crohn disease limited to the colon
distractor_notes: Lactose intolerance causes osmotic symptoms after lactose ingestion but does not explain positive tissue transglutaminase antibodies and iron deficiency from mucosal injury.
Colonic Crohn disease does not typically produce celiac serology and proximal small-bowel malabsorption.
Chronic pancreatitis causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and steatorrhea but not positive celiac autoantibodies.
Irritable bowel syndrome does not cause weight loss, iron deficiency anemia, or positive autoimmune serology.
key_expl: Chronic malabsorptive symptoms, iron deficiency, and strongly positive tissue transglutaminase IgA are classic for celiac disease.
objective: Diagnose celiac disease from malabsorptive symptoms plus characteristic serologic evidence.
clues: chronic diarrhea with iron deficiency anemia

sources.title: Celiac Disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes celiac disease as immune-mediated small-intestinal injury triggered by gluten and diagnosed with serologic testing and intestinal evaluation.

sources.title: Celiac disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes diarrhea, weight loss, nutrient deficiencies, and celiac antibody testing.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease produces skip lesions, fistulas, strictures, and can involve any part of the gastrointestinal tract, commonly the terminal ileum.
vignette: A 24-year-old man has chronic nonbloody diarrhea, right lower quadrant abdominal pain, weight loss, and a draining perianal fistula. Colonoscopy shows patchy inflammation of the terminal ileum and colon with areas of normal mucosa between lesions.
distractor_notes: Ulcerative colitis causes continuous mucosal inflammation beginning in the rectum and does not typically produce transmural perianal fistulas.
Celiac disease primarily causes small-intestinal malabsorption and does not cause skip lesions or fistulas.
Irritable bowel syndrome does not cause objective inflammatory lesions, weight loss, or fistula formation.
Appendicitis is an acute focal process and does not explain chronic diarrhea with patchy ileocolitis and perianal disease.
key_expl: Transmural skip lesions involving terminal ileum plus a perianal fistula are classic for Crohn disease.
objective: Differentiate Crohn disease from ulcerative colitis using transmural fistulizing disease and skip lesions.
clues: patchy terminal ileal and colonic inflammation

sources.title: Crohn's Disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes Crohn disease as chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any GI segment and cause fistulas and strictures.

sources.title: Crohn's disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and fistula formation in Crohn disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Reduced UGT1A1 activity mildly impairs hepatic bilirubin glucuronidation, producing intermittent isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia that can worsen with fasting or illness.
vignette: A healthy 21-year-old man develops mild scleral icterus while fasting before an examination. Total bilirubin is mildly elevated with a predominantly unconjugated fraction; aminotransferases and alkaline phosphatase are normal.
lead: Reduced activity of which enzyme best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Heme oxygenase generates biliverdin during heme breakdown; reduced activity would not cause isolated impaired bilirubin conjugation.
Biliverdin reductase converts biliverdin to bilirubin and is not the deficient enzyme in Gilbert syndrome.
Ferrochelatase catalyzes insertion of iron into protoporphyrin during heme synthesis.
Glucose-6-phosphatase is deficient in glycogen storage disease type I and is unrelated to bilirubin conjugation.
key_expl: Gilbert syndrome reflects partial reduction in UGT1A1-mediated bilirubin conjugation, causing mild intermittent unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
objective: Explain benign fasting-associated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in Gilbert syndrome through reduced UGT1A1 activity.
clues: triggered by fasting in an otherwise healthy adult

sources.title: Gilbert syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Gilbert syndrome as reduced bilirubin-processing capacity due to UGT1A1 variants, causing intermittent unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

sources.title: UGT1A1 gene
sources.support: UGT1A1 encodes bilirubin UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, which conjugates bilirubin in hepatocytes.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Aldolase B deficiency prevents cleavage of fructose-1-phosphate, trapping phosphate and inhibiting hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis after fructose ingestion.
vignette: A 7-month-old infant develops vomiting, diaphoresis, lethargy, and hepatomegaly shortly after fruit juice is introduced. Blood glucose is low.
lead: Which reaction is most directly impaired?
correct: Fructose-1-phosphate to glyceraldehyde and dihydroxyacetone phosphate
distractor_notes: Fructokinase catalyzes fructose phosphorylation; isolated fructokinase deficiency causes benign essential fructosuria.
Galactose-1-phosphate metabolism is impaired in classic galactosemia.
Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type I.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes phenylketonuria.
key_expl: Aldolase B cleaves fructose-1-phosphate into glyceraldehyde and DHAP; deficiency causes hereditary fructose intolerance.
objective: Relate fructose-triggered hypoglycemia and liver dysfunction to aldolase B deficiency.

sources.title: Hereditary fructose intolerance
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes hereditary fructose intolerance as ALDOB deficiency causing toxic fructose-1-phosphate accumulation after fructose ingestion.

sources.title: ALDOB gene
sources.support: ALDOB encodes aldolase B, which cleaves fructose-1-phosphate during hepatic fructose metabolism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Certain misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin variants polymerize and accumulate within hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum, causing toxic gain-of-function liver injury.
vignette: A 6-year-old child with severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency has persistent elevation of aminotransferases. Liver biopsy shows eosinophilic globules within hepatocytes that are PAS positive and diastase resistant.
lead: Which mechanism most directly causes the liver injury?
correct: Intracellular accumulation of misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin in hepatocytes
distractors: Unopposed neutrophil elastase acting directly on hepatocytes
Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts
distractor_notes: Unopposed neutrophil elastase explains emphysema in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency but not the characteristic hepatocyte inclusion injury.
Copper accumulation is the mechanism of Wilson disease.
Iron overload is characteristic of hereditary hemochromatosis.
Autoimmune bile-duct injury occurs in cholestatic autoimmune disorders and is not the mechanism of SERPINA1-associated liver disease.
key_expl: The liver disease of severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency results from retention and polymerization of abnormal protein within hepatocytes.
objective: Distinguish the toxic protein-accumulation mechanism of alpha-1 antitrypsin liver disease from the loss-of-antiprotease mechanism causing emphysema.

sources.title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes abnormal alpha-1 antitrypsin accumulation in liver cells as a cause of liver damage.

sources.title: SERPINA1 gene
sources.locator: Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes
sources.support: SERPINA1 variants can cause misfolded alpha-1 antitrypsin to accumulate in hepatocytes and injure the liver.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Gain-of-function PRSS1 variants increase inappropriate intrapancreatic trypsin activity, promoting premature digestive-enzyme activation, recurrent pancreatic autodigestion, and chronic pancreatitis.
vignette: A 15-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back since childhood. Several relatives are similarly affected. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic PRSS1 variant.
lead: Which molecular abnormality most directly promotes pancreatic injury?
correct: Premature activation or persistence of trypsin within the pancreas
distractors: Failure of pancreatic bicarbonate secretion due to isolated secretin receptor loss
Complete absence of pancreatic lipase synthesis only
distractor_notes: Bicarbonate abnormalities can affect pancreatic secretions but are not the defining PRSS1 gain-of-function mechanism of hereditary pancreatitis.
Isolated lipase absence would cause fat malabsorption but not recurrent autodigestive pancreatitis.
Bile acid conjugation occurs in the liver and does not explain PRSS1-associated pancreatitis.
Lactase deficiency causes lactose intolerance, not pancreatic inflammation.
key_expl: PRSS1 encodes cationic trypsinogen; pathogenic activating variants promote excessive intrapancreatic trypsin activity and autodigestion.
objective: Explain hereditary pancreatitis through inappropriate intrapancreatic trypsin activation caused by PRSS1 variants.
clues: autosomal dominant family history with PRSS1 variant

sources.title: Hereditary pancreatitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes hereditary pancreatitis as recurrent pancreatic inflammation commonly caused by PRSS1 variants that alter trypsin regulation.

sources.title: PRSS1 gene
sources.support: PRSS1 encodes cationic trypsinogen, and pathogenic variants can increase inappropriate trypsin activity within the pancreas.
